input_values.description: REPLACE the instance's inputs with this WHOLE set -- it is not a patch. Read the current ones from terrapod_catalog_instance_get and send them back with your change applied: a required field left out is refused 422 rather than keeping its stored value, and a key that is not a form field is refused too. Omit the field entirely to keep the stored set unchanged, which is how a version-pin-only reconfigure is expressed

version_pin.description: pin this instance to a module version. OMIT to keep its current pin; pass EMPTY to make it FLOAT, which resolves to the module's latest uploaded version now and at every later reconfigure. So empty is a change of tracking mode rather than a cleared field

workspace_id.description: the instance's workspace id (ws-... or a bare UUID)

allowed_agent_pool_ids.description: restrict provisioning to these agent pools (apool-... or a bare UUID). OMIT to permit any pool the provisioner can assign, which is the default. An EMPTY LIST is not the same as omitting it: it permits no pool at all, so every provision is then refused 403

ansible_directory.description: the subdirectory OF THE MODULE that holds the Ansible configuration. At provision its whole subtree is COPIED into the generated configuration version at the same relative path -- not referenced from it, because a composite run's configure Job re-fetches the configuration version and never runs init, so there is no .terraform/modules/ for it to point at. The provisioned workspace's config_directory is then this same path. Relative to the module root and stored BYTE FOR BYTE: a leading or trailing slash, a '..' segment, leading or trailing whitespace, or more than 255 characters are each REFUSED (422) rather than cleaned up, because the value round-trips through the Terraform provider and silently storing a different one than you sent fails the apply with 'Provider produced inconsistent result after apply'. Three further refusals land at PROVISION rather than here: the module has no uploaded version to copy from; this names the module ROOT (empty, '.', or a trailing slash) rather than a subdirectory; or the subtree holds no regular file, in which case the error names what the module does ship. Only regular files are copied -- a symlink, hard link or device entry is dropped, because this repacks into a tarball a runner extracts

configure_enabled.description: whether the workspace this item provisions has an ANSIBLE CONFIGURE operation. DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so a Terraform-only item says nothing here. This says WHETHER; ansible_directory says WHERE, and the path does NOT carry off in its emptiness. Setting this true with no ansible_directory is REFUSED (422): it is incoherent rather than a no-op, because it would provision a workspace whose Ansible root is the configuration version's root, where only the generated wrapper lives, and fail at run time for want of a playbook

default_limit.description: the ansible --limit templated onto the provisioned workspace as its default_limit, overridable per run. EMPTY MEANS THE WHOLE INVENTORY, which is ansible's own default -- so this is the blast radius of every triggered configure on the instances this item creates, and naming a canary group here is what bounds them. Stored byte for byte; leading or trailing whitespace is refused (422) rather than stripped

default_playbook.description: the playbook templated onto the provisioned workspace as its default_playbook, relative to ansible_directory. Empty means the workspace gets no default and every configure run on it must name its own playbook. Same byte-for-byte validation as ansible_directory: no leading or trailing slash, no '..', no stray whitespace, 255 characters at most, each refused rather than normalised

default_version_pin.description: pin every provision to this module version. OMIT OR PASS EMPTY TO FLOAT, which resolves to the module's latest uploaded version at each provision and reconfigure -- so leaving it empty is a deliberate tracking choice rather than an unset field

description.description: what this item provisions, for the person choosing it

enabled.description: whether the item may be provisioned from. DEFAULTS TO TRUE, so an ordinary item says nothing here. An item with this false is still published and readable but refuses to provision (409), which is how one is retired without deleting it and orphaning its instances

apply_only.description: withhold this variable from a plan and deliver it to an apply AND to an Ansible configure; default false. A plan executes the configuration's code, so a credential only the apply needs should not be in a plan's environment; a configure runs the repository's playbooks against real hosts, so it receives apply-only rows too. To withhold a variable from an apply as well, use configure_only instead. For a different value per phase, set TWO variables with the same key — one ordinary, one apply_only — and the apply-only one wins on an apply

category.description: terraform, env, git_http_auth, git_ssh_auth, ansible_machine_auth or ansible_vault_auth (default terraform); native is accepted as an equivalent name for terraform. terraform is the engine's own parameter channel -- Terraform input variables, Pulumi stack config, Ansible extra vars -- one category, delivered by whichever engine the workspace runs; Terrapod's own API calls it native, and this tool reads the compatibility surface, which calls it terraform. The other four are credential categories: the value is a JSON envelope rather than a literal, all four are always sensitive whatever you ask for, and none accepts an OpenBao/Vault value source. In the two ansible_* categories the key is the credential's NAME. For ansible_machine_auth the INVENTORY says where it is used, with a ${terrapod:<name>.<field>} placeholder the runner substitutes while rendering, so it can fill any connection variable; for ansible_vault_auth the name is also the vault ID label

configure_only.description: withhold this variable from a plan AND from an apply, delivering it only to an Ansible configure; default false. For the fleet's own credential — an SSH private key to the estate, a become password — which nothing in a plan or an apply has any business holding. A THIRD slot rather than a variant of apply_only, because apply_only already means apply AND configure, so it cannot express withholding from an apply too. Setting both apply_only and configure_only is REFUSED by the server with a 422 rather than resolved

hcl.description: deprecated alias for structured; both are the same flag

sensitive.description: mark sensitive — masked at rest and in responses; default false

structured.description: the value is a typed expression rather than a plain string (lists/objects/numbers/bools); default false

value.description: the value (empty is legal, e.g. flag-shaped env vars)

value_source.description: static (default — value is the literal) or vault, where value is a JSON reference {"mount":…,"path":…,"field":…} that Terrapod reads from OpenBao (or HashiCorp Vault) at run time; a vault-sourced variable is always sensitive and the secret is never stored in Terrapod. Add "file":{"name":"gcp/adc.json"} to the reference to deliver the secret as a file on the runner: the variable then holds the file's absolute path (usable as file(var.x), or by a tool reading a path from an env var). name defaults to the key; a relative name lands under /var/run/terrapod/files/, a name starting ~/ in the runner's home (e.g. ~/.aws/credentials). Not allowed with structured=true (or its alias hcl=true). The file's content is exactly one of: the reference's field (add "encoding":"base64" inside file to decode it to UTF-8 text); "template" inside file with no field, a logic-less template over the one read such as "[default]\naws_access_key_id = {{ access_key }}\n" (dotted names reach into maps; filters json, base64decode, trim, lines, indent N; _lease.ttl, _lease.renewable, _lease.expires_at when the secret has a lease; at most 16 KiB); or "format" inside file with no field, json or env for the whole secret, optionally narrowed by "fields":[...]

allow_fork_pr_plans.description: allow a pull request opened from a FORK to get a speculative plan. **Off by default**, which is the safe setting: such a plan runs the fork author's code with this workspace's full credential set (env variables, secret-manager values, git credentials, the runner's cloud identity), and that author has no write access and cannot merge, so the plan is the only path by which their code reaches those credentials. Pull requests from branches in the repository itself always plan and are unaffected. Set it true only on a workspace that holds nothing worth taking, and note that an autodiscovery rule carries its own value for the workspaces it creates (GHSA-gp5w-76rw-c452)

ansible_collections.description: the ansible collections installed before a configure runs, declared on the platform. Each entry is {"name": "namespace.name"} with an optional "version" (a pin or a range, as in ansible's own requirements.yml; omit for whatever resolves). These are installed AFTER the configuration's own requirements.yml and with --force, so an entry here OVERRIDES the repository's build of that collection and leaves every other one standing. Collections come from this deployment's own Galaxy surface -- its published ones and a pull-through proxy of upstream -- so source and type are deliberately not settable. ROLES are a different mechanism and are not declared here: they come from git, using the workspace's git credentials, declared in the configuration's own requirements.yml

version.description: version or range; omit for whatever resolves

ansible_execution_environment.description: label of one of the deployment's own execution environments; OVERRIDES ansible_version when set, so the line is then ignored; omit or empty to use the built-in image for the line

ansible_version.description: ansible-core LINE whose execution environment this workspace's configure operations run in, e.g. 2.21; an exact patch is accepted and names its own line; omit or empty to inherit the deployment default

auto_apply_mode.description: conditional auto-apply: never, always, create (only plans that add resources), create_update (also in-place updates). create and create_update never auto-apply a destroy or replace. Set this OR auto_apply, not both.

auto_configure_enabled.description: whether a PUSH that changes this workspace's ansible config root queues a configure. DEFAULTS TO FALSE. It runs the workspace's default_playbook against its default_limit, because a push carries no run options -- which is also what BOUNDS it: a workspace whose default_limit names a canary group cannot be made to fire wider by a git push. Needs configure_enabled; without it this is inert

config_directory.description: the directory the ansible CONFIGURE operation runs in, relative to the configuration version's root: its fetch scope and the working directory both the inventory resolver and the playbook executor run from. An ordinary path, exactly like working_directory -- empty or omitted means the configuration version's ROOT, and a subdirectory means rooted there. It does NOT declare whether the workspace HAS a configure operation: configure_enabled does (#1966), so setting this alone turns nothing on, and leaving it empty on a configure-enabled workspace is the ordinary way to say "at the root" rather than a missing value. Distinct from working_directory, which is the terraform/pulumi root; one repository can have both, at different directories

configure_after_apply.description: whether an APPLY on this workspace is followed by a configure ON THE SAME RUN. DEFAULTS TO FALSE. It is a workspace setting rather than a per-run option because the terraform/tofu CLI cannot pass one, and keeping the configure attached to the run means a remote execution keeps streaming its logs. The host set still comes from the inventory and the limit from default_limit -- the apply decides only WHEN. A DESTROY apply never chains one. Needs configure_enabled

configure_all_hosts.description: whether a DERIVED configure -- one an inventory change or an apply produced, rather than one somebody asked for with a limit -- targets EVERY host rather than only the hosts that changed. DEFAULTS TO FALSE, which narrows. Narrowing is conditioned on what justifies breadth: new playbook or role code has to reach every host, while a changed HOST is no reason to touch the others, so a derived configure narrows when the ansible code under config_directory is unchanged since the last successful configure and goes wide when it moved. This flag is the override and it WIDENS -- a flag someone forgets leaves you configuring more, not less. It does not affect a configure you create with an explicit limit, which targets what you asked for

configure_enabled.description: whether this workspace has an ansible CONFIGURE operation. DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so the operation is opt-in and this is what turns it on -- setting config_directory alone does NOT (#1966), and a workspace with configure_enabled false has no configure operation and no ansible inventory however its roots are set. With it true, config_directory says WHERE the operation runs and inventory_paths says what it targets. Independent of plan_apply_enabled, so a workspace may have both; both off is refused (422)

default_limit.description: the default --limit for a configure run, overridable per run. Empty means the whole inventory, which is ansible's own default. This narrows which HOSTS a run touches and is the configure operation's equivalent of -target on a plan

default_playbook.description: the playbook a configure run executes unless the run names another, the way vcs_ref overrides vcs_branch on a run. Relative to config_directory. Empty means the workspace has no default and every configure run must name its playbook

dynamic_inventory_enabled.description: permit ansible's auto inventory plugin -- a DECLARED plugin config, which is a YAML file carrying a top-level plugin: key -- for this workspace's configure operations. DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so a workspace that says nothing refuses plugin sources. The API NEVER executes a plugin in either state: with it off the API refuses a plugin source BY NAME rather than resolving the other sources and reporting the short host set that results as the truth, and with it on the API SKIPS that source and says so per source, leaving the RUNNER to re-resolve the inventory as the authoritative answer. Independent of inventory_scripts_enabled on purpose, so declared configs can be permitted without also permitting arbitrary executables: a declared config is inspectable and names a collection that can be pinned and installed, where a script names nothing. Only meaningful with configure_enabled

engine.description: the execution engine family: terraform (default) or another engine this deployment enables, such as pulumi. NOT execution_backend, which picks tofu vs terraform within the Terraform engine. Workspaces are created here, in the UI or with the Terraform provider — never by an engine's own CLI

engine_version.description: version of the engine this workspace runs; partial like 1.15 (means 1.15.*), no HCL operators

execution_backend.description: which binary runs a Terraform-engine workspace: tofu or terraform. A choice WITHIN the Terraform engine — Pulumi has one binary, so this has no meaning on a pulumi workspace (default: server default)

inventory_paths.description: the ansible inventory sources, each a FILE or a DIRECTORY relative to the repository root. ORDERED -- the order IS the precedence ansible applies, so this is a list and not a set, and reordering it changes which value wins. Name the files or directories you mean rather than a parent: -i over a directory holding both production and staging MERGES them into one inventory, which is how a staging workspace ends up carrying production hosts. Pass an empty list to remove every source

inventory_scripts_enabled.description: permit ansible's script inventory plugin -- an EXECUTABLE inventory script -- for this workspace's configure operations. DEFAULTS TO FALSE. The API NEVER executes a script in either state: with it off the API refuses such a source BY NAME rather than resolving partially and reporting a short host set as the truth, and with it on the API skips it, leaving the RUNNER to re-resolve and be authoritative. The STRICTER of the two switches and deliberately separate from dynamic_inventory_enabled: a script carries no config to read and nothing to pin, so permitting declared plugin configs does not imply permitting executables, and on the runner the environment is the only control because a committed script arrives executable. Only meaningful with configure_enabled

labels.description: key/value labels for RBAC + filtering (reserved keys rejected)

name.description: the workspace name (unique within the org)

oidc_audiences.description: the per-provider audiences this workspace's run identity tokens are minted with -- its cloud identity opt-in (#1901). Omit it (the default) and the workspace overrides nothing, inheriting the deployment's catalogue; a deployment that configures no audiences mints nothing and its runs authenticate with the agent pool's own identity, exactly as before. A MAP keyed on the provider configuration a token is for, never a flat list: the bare provider type exactly as a provider block writes it (aws, vault), or type.alias for one aliased configuration (aws.west). The alias is part of the KEY -- do not split on the dot and do not fold aws.west into aws; they are separate targets, and the runner asks for whichever its configuration actually uses. Each value is ALWAYS a list even for a single entry, because a federation target's audience is one value and a list of several is a deliberate these-are-interchangeable statement; the runner mints one token per target carrying only that target's audiences. An audience is an opaque string the federation target itself names -- whatever your cloud's or secret store's trust configuration expects -- and Terrapod stores it verbatim; nothing here is specific to any one cloud, because Terrapod only mints an OIDC JWT and the runner writes it to a file. What you pass is this workspace's OVERRIDE, merged per key OVER the deployment's own catalogue, so naming one target does not restate the rest. The read side differs and this is the trap: a workspace reports its oidc-audiences as the MERGED view, so writing back what you read would promote every inherited entry into an override. A key whose list is EMPTY is refused (422) -- express no-audiences-for-this-target by leaving the key out, which falls back to the deployment's value, because an empty list is indistinguishable from a typo. A token audienced for two targets is replayable between them, so give a target only its own audiences. Setting this does NOT by itself grant anything: the federation target's own trust policy decides what a token bearing these audiences may do.

owner_email.description: workspace owner email (defaults to the caller)

plan_apply_enabled.description: whether this workspace has a PLAN/APPLY operation -- the terraform, tofu or pulumi lifecycle. DEFAULTS TO TRUE, so omit it for an ordinary infrastructure workspace. Pass false only for a configure-only workspace, and pass configure_enabled=true in the same call when you do: both operations off is refused (422), because a workspace that can do nothing is not a state anyone wants -- lock the workspace instead, which parks it reversibly. Independent of configure_enabled, so a workspace may have both

pulumi_bind_plan.description: Pulumi workspaces only: bind the update to the approved preview (preview --save-plan then up --plan). Off by default; setting it true is rejected on any other engine

terraform_version.description: the same version under its original name; prefer engine_version. Setting both to different values is rejected

vcs_connection_id.description: VCS connection id to wire this workspace to a repo

workspace_id.description: the workspace id (ws-...) to delete

workspace.description: the workspace id (ws-...) or its name

engine.description: return only workspaces on this execution engine: terraform or pulumi. Omit for every engine. Narrow with this before doing anything that assumes one engine — the tools differ by engine

page_size.description: max workspaces to return in this page (default 50)

agent_pool_id.description: agent pool id (apool-...); assigns exactly one pool, REPLACING any existing set. Mutually exclusive with agent_pool_ids

agent_pool_ids.description: replace the workspace''s agent-pool set (apool-...). Flat set — every pool is equally eligible to claim a run. Mutually exclusive with agent_pool_id

ai_policy_mode.description: this workspace's override for the AI POLICY GATE -- whether a run's plan is reviewed by a model before it may apply: enabled, disabled or inherit. inherit defers to the deployment setting, which is the default and is NOT the same as disabled. Omit to leave the stored value alone. Distinct from ai_summary_mode: the gate can BLOCK a run, the summary only describes one

ai_summary_context.description: workspace-specific facts given to the model on top of the deployment's own context -- what this estate is for, naming conventions, which resources are load-bearing. Prose, not configuration: it changes what a summary SAYS, never what a run does. A hint rather than a repository, and capped at 4000 characters. Omitting the field leaves the stored value alone; pass an EMPTY STRING to clear it

ai_summary_mode.description: this workspace's override for AI PLAN SUMMARIES -- prose describing what a plan will do, which blocks nothing: enabled, disabled or inherit. inherit defers to the deployment setting. Omit to leave the stored value alone

allow_fork_pr_plans.description: allow a pull request opened from a FORK to get a speculative plan. **Off by default**, which is the safe setting: such a plan runs the fork author's code with this workspace's full credential set (env variables, secret-manager values, git credentials, the runner's cloud identity), and that author has no write access and cannot merge, so the plan is the only path by which their code reaches those credentials. Pull requests from branches in the repository itself always plan and are unaffected. Set it true only on a workspace that holds nothing worth taking, and note that an autodiscovery rule carries its own value for the workspaces it creates (GHSA-gp5w-76rw-c452)

ansible_collections.description: the ansible collections installed before a configure runs, declared on the platform. Each entry is {"name": "namespace.name"} with an optional "version" (a pin or a range, as in ansible's own requirements.yml; omit for whatever resolves). These are installed AFTER the configuration's own requirements.yml and with --force, so an entry here OVERRIDES the repository's build of that collection and leaves every other one standing. Collections come from this deployment's own Galaxy surface -- its published ones and a pull-through proxy of upstream -- so source and type are deliberately not settable. ROLES are a different mechanism and are not declared here: they come from git, using the workspace's git credentials, declared in the configuration's own requirements.yml. Omitting the field leaves the stored list alone; pass an empty list to clear it

version.description: version or range; omit for whatever resolves

ansible_execution_environment.description: label of one of the deployment's own execution environments; OVERRIDES ansible_version when set, so the line is then ignored. OMIT to leave the stored value alone; pass an empty string to CLEAR it, after which the built-in image for the line is used again

ansible_version.description: ansible-core LINE whose execution environment this workspace's configure operations run in, e.g. 2.21; an exact patch is accepted and names its own line; omit or empty to inherit the deployment default

auto_merge.description: merge the pull request once every workspace it affects has reached its required state. Omit to leave the stored value alone

auto_merge_strategy.description: how auto_merge merges: merge, squash or rebase. Only meaningful with auto_merge true. Omit to leave the stored value alone

debug_mode.description: hold this workspace's FAILED runner pods open for inspection rather than letting them be cleaned up. drift_detection_enabled.description: whether Terrapod plans this workspace on a schedule to detect drift -- infrastructure that no longer matches the recorded state. A drift run is plan-only and never applies. Omit to leave the stored value alone

drift_detection_interval_seconds.description: how often a drift check runs, in seconds; 86400 (daily) by default. Only meaningful with drift_detection_enabled true. Omit to leave the stored value alone

drift_ignore_rules.description: resource addresses or attribute paths whose drift is not reported -- for the perpetual phantom diffs a provider produces on write-only attributes. Pass an empty list to remove every rule; omitting the field leaves the stored list alone

dynamic_inventory_enabled.description: turn ansible's auto inventory plugin -- a DECLARED plugin config, which is a YAML file carrying a top-level plugin: key -- on or off for this workspace. A run SNAPSHOTS both switches at creation, so changing this cannot move the answer under a run already in flight

ee_resource_cpu.description: CPU request for the Ansible EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT -- the sidecar container a configure run's playbooks execute in -- not the orchestrator, which resource_cpu sizes. Same quantity rules and the same 2x limit. EMPTY means this workspace takes the deployment default rather than sizing the environment itself, so passing an empty string is how a workspace rejoins that default; omitting the field leaves the stored value alone

ee_resource_memory.description: memory request for the Ansible execution-environment sidecar. Limit is 2x. Empty takes the deployment default. See ee_resource_cpu

engine_version.description: version of the engine this workspace runs; partial like 1.15 (means 1.15.*)

execution_backend.description: which binary runs a Terraform-engine workspace: tofu or terraform. A choice WITHIN the Terraform engine — Pulumi has one binary, so this has no meaning on a pulumi workspace

labels.description: replace the label set (reserved keys rejected)

oidc_audiences.description: replace this workspace's per-provider audience overrides for its run identity tokens -- its cloud identity opt-in (#1901). Omitting the field leaves the existing overrides alone; pass an EMPTY object to clear every one of them, which drops the workspace back to inheriting the deployment's catalogue wholesale. The alias is part of the KEY -- do not split on the dot and do not fold aws.west into aws; they are separate targets, and the runner asks for whichever its configuration actually uses. Each value is ALWAYS a list even for a single entry, because a federation target's audience is one value and a list of several is a deliberate these-are-interchangeable statement; the runner mints one token per target carrying only that target's audiences. parallelism.description: the engine's -parallelism for this workspace's runs; 10 by default, which is the engine's own. Lower it for a provider that rate-limits; raising it rarely helps and can trip API quotas. Omit to leave the stored value alone

plan_apply_enabled.description: turn this workspace's PLAN/APPLY operation -- the terraform, tofu or pulumi lifecycle -- on or off. Omitting the field leaves the stored value alone. Turning it off is refused (422) unless the workspace has, or this same call gives it, a configure operation: the refusal is checked against the MERGED row, so passing plan_apply_enabled=false alone on an ordinary workspace fails rather than leaving it able to do nothing. Lock the workspace instead to park it reversibly. Independent of configure_enabled

plan_expiry_seconds.description: how long an apply-capable plan may wait for confirmation before it is expired; unset means never, which is the default. It does NOT expire speculative plans. Omit to leave the stored value alone

pulumi_bind_plan.description: Pulumi workspaces only: bind the update to the approved preview (preview --save-plan then up --plan). Off by default; rejected on any other engine

resource_cpu.description: CPU request for this workspace's runner Jobs, as a Kubernetes quantity: a whole number of CPUs (1, 4) or millicores (500m). The LIMIT is twice this, computed automatically. Decimals (0.5) and decimal SI suffixes are refused (422), because the limit is 2x the request and those forms cannot be doubled -- accepting one would silently leave the limit equal to the request. Omit to leave the stored value alone

resource_memory.description: memory request for this workspace's runner Jobs, as a Kubernetes quantity in binary bytes (256Mi, 2Gi). Limit is 2x. Same refusals as resource_cpu

security_scan_enforcement.description: what a security-scan finding DOES: off (do not scan at all), advisory (report and let the run continue) or enforced (hold the apply until the finding is overridden). Distinct from security_scan_severity_threshold, which decides what is REPORTED rather than what blocks. A workspace whose engine produces no Terraform plan JSON -- a pulumi one -- accepts only off, because a scanner has nothing to read there. Omit to leave the stored value alone

security_scan_engine.description: which scanner reviews a plan: checkov or trivy. Omit to leave the stored value alone

security_scan_severity_threshold.description: the lowest severity a scan finding must reach to be reported: critical, high, medium or low. This is what gets REPORTED, not what blocks -- security_scan_enforcement is the separate setting that decides that. Omit to leave the stored value alone

security_scan_skip_rules.description: scanner rule ids this workspace does not report, as the scanner itself names them (e.g. CKV_AWS_18). Pass an empty list to remove every skip; omitting the field leaves the stored list alone

slack_channel.description: the Slack channel this workspace's run notifications go to, overriding the deployment default. Pass an EMPTY STRING to drop back to the default; omitting the field leaves the stored value alone

terraform_version.description: the same version under its original name; prefer engine_version. Setting both to different values is rejected

terragrunt_enabled.description: run this workspace through terragrunt rather than the engine binary directly. Omit to leave the stored value alone

terragrunt_version.description: which terragrunt version this workspace runs; only meaningful with terragrunt_enabled true. Omit to leave the stored value alone

trigger_prefixes.description: the repository paths that make a push or pull request create a run here, each a directory prefix from the repository root. It REPLACES working_directory for the trigger decision and UNIONS with it for the fetch, so a monorepo workspace watching several directories names them all. A push touching no matching path creates no run at all. Pass an empty list to remove every prefix, which falls back to working_directory; omitting the field leaves the stored list alone

var_files.description: .tfvars files from the repository, applied in order, relative to the working directory. Pass an empty list to remove every one; omitting the field leaves the stored list alone

vcs_workflow.description: when a pull request's run applies: merge_then_apply (the default -- the PR gets a speculative plan, and the apply happens after it merges) or apply_then_merge (the PR's plan is applied BEFORE the merge, which holds the workspace lock while the PR is open and is what Atlantis does). Omit to leave the stored value alone

workspace_id.description: the workspace id (ws-...) to update
the workspace id (ws-...) whose variable sets to list
